description:
The df129d9e holistic review on 2026-11-08 (second run) found that whole-repository `jit validate` still breaks @/issue/df129d9e/decision/D-03, the findings-stderr rule that REQ-09's output contract relies on. `crates/jit/src/dispatch/validate.rs` puts the full repository-integrity error into the findings message. For derived-state drift, `crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs` builds that error as a multi-line list. The shared emitter then writes every line of it to stderr. 75a90224 fixed the same defect for `--branch-drift` and `--leases`, and its D-01 records that `error.message` is the one-line summary, while the details live in the report and in `error.details`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: When whole-repository `jit validate` finds a repository-integrity error, including derived-state drift alone or together with rule errors, human mode prints the error's full details in the stdout report and exactly one summary line on stderr. Under `--json`, `error.details` carries the full integrity error, `error.message` is the one-line summary, and the exit code is unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every `Outcome::findings` call site under `crates/jit/src/dispatch/` passes a message that cannot contain a newline. A site whose message could carry multi-line content moves that content into its report, which renders on stdout and serializes under `--json`. The return lists each site with its verdict.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each path this issue changes has a test of its streams at the cheapest layer that observes them, including the drift path. No assertion is weakened, and no property owned elsewhere is re-proved.
- [hard] REQ-04: Docs and the CHANGELOG describe any JSON- or human-visible change, with each fact in its one canonical home (@/charter/D-13).
title: Every findings outcome prints a one-line stderr summary
